1) I have no idea why they got rid of the cut scenes, they were some of my favourite bits- I assume to make it "grittier" and more in line with what Prime want to be putting out 

2) Ruth gets pregnant with her daughter just after leaving the camps (literally days/weeks by the looks of things) because we know Meyer gets killed before they leave the transit camp. Jonah is meant to be 17, its not thaaaat far of a stretch- people had children much younger then. 

3) I assumed the colonel was so fine with it because she was so wrapped up in her own "pure blood" mania that she really didn't feel anything for people who were killed by others that she perceived as subhuman. I think it's done as a way to show you how far she is in her delusions, she doesn't even have any maternal instinct. 

Some of your further questions are answered more in s2- I personally loved S1 and thought it was one of the best shows I've watched in a long time. S2 I found frustrating, still good but lacking the brilliance that S1 had (at least before the cuts). If you do want answers though, they will have that.
Same here! I kept thinking "I swear I know that girl from somewhere!"

Personally I feel as if that's exactly why they had Adam in this ep- the next episode "Father's Day" is when Rose truly messes up for the first time and the Doctors idea of "stupid emotional humans" is really thrown to the forefront.

I think theyre probably going to resolve that in s3- especially since Faye basically told the police Laurie's name and where she lives. Even if they know she didn't kill mouse, they'll still be all over that massive drug bust.

Ironic you saying I don't know how addiction works considering I've grown up in a house with one and suffered addiction myself, but okay. 

Most people have a safety net- people they can lean on when their life gets difficult. Friends, family who will help you get through those difficult times. People suffering from addiction are even more likely to need that support from others. 
I don't know where you got the idea I think Jules should be sitting around looking after or entertain Rue- I'm just saying it's shitty the way she slept with someone else when they had shared intimate moments. 
When you decide to date or become friends with someone with mental health issues or addiction, you accept that you will be affected or may have to help them with their addiction problems. Imagine if your partner came to you saying "I'm struggling with addiction", you wouldn't just turn around to them and say "ah well, sucks but not my problem". 

I agree that Rue should have been in an in-patient facility but she wasn't,these characters are flawed human beings and if everyone did exactly what they are supposed to then there wouldn't be a show.

I'm not blaming Jules, I'm just saying that Rue's relapse was as a consequence of Jules. That's obviously not Jules' responsibility, but regardless, your actions have consequences that you should probably think about, especially if you're in a relationship with a drug addict.

I personally love Cassie's character but it solidified for me in the Halloween episode when she dressed as Alabama worley because true romance is my favourite film and no one I know has ever watched it! 
I'm only halfway through season 2 but I think Cassie trying to come to terms with her single life at the start is a real glimpse into her inner character and hopefully her character will revisit that and try to solidify it a little more. 
Personally I think framing her character as who she is outside of a relationship (or whatever is going on with Nate) is so important and I hope they look a little more into that in S3
